question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.
answer: Yes — motorist (vehicle-occupant) deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, a 26% drop, and since the file has no miles-driven data I solved for it: per-mile risk only fails to decline if 2025 driving was below ~74% of 2013's mileage, so with NYC driving roughly back to pre-pandemic levels the risk of a motorist being killed per mile is about a quarter lower than in 2013 (the 2020–21 spike and the post-2019 halving of minor-crash reports — injury counts stayed flat — are the caveats).
